summary: Interpreted the healing-phase successor receipt and opened the other registered question with a filed experiment. Receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 parsed four events and evaluated all ten comparisons: the carried seven reproduce the split-brain window (violated at indices 1 and 2, controls holding), and both new healed-phase assertions are violated at event index 3 — the nodes still hold different payloads at conflict index 11 with the same term 3 (A and C minority-write against B, D and E majority-write), and the restarted node still reports {A,B,C} after the cluster is whole and committing, with its log advancing to 12 as the progress control. That resolves the child question's post-healing limitation; its disposition is now explained and its rationale, the parent account and the joint history across the three receipts were rewritten, with the parent's persistence limitation narrowed to long-run/repair-path coverage and the healed-leader variance recorded as counterevidence. A new fact records why such same-term divergence is never reconciled by AppendEntries (truncation needs a term difference; same-term duplicates are skipped). Finally, I filed an experiment for the registered constructor question: one node with a snapshot at index 1000 and 9000 committed LogCommand entries staged as commit index 10000, constructed with the feature off and on, which locally showed the feature-off control returning with lastApplied still at 1000 while the feature-on constructor never returned within the 5s window — the first fixture attempt with LogNoop entries returned in both modes, which is why the entries were moved to the commit path. Incomplete: that experiment's receipt and interpretation, the no-feature restart control inside the cluster, and whether a snapshot install or compaction eventually repairs the divergent entries.
